import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Normality of Irrational Algebraic Numbers

It is unknown whether every irrational algebraic real number is normal in any integer base.
The stronger conjecture that every irrational algebraic real number is absolutely normal is stated
separately: normality in one base and normality in every base are not equivalent definitions.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Normal number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number)
- [BC01] Bailey, David H., and Richard E. Crandall. "On the random character of fundamental constant
  expansions." Experimental Mathematics 10.2 (2001): 175-190.
  https://projecteuclid.org/journals/experimental-mathematics/volume-10/issue-2/On-the-random-character-of-fundamental-constant-expansions/em/999188630.full
-/

open NormalNumber

namespace AlgebraicNormality

/-- A real number is irrational algebraic if it is algebraic over `ℚ` but not rational. -/
def IsIrrationalAlgebraic (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsAlgebraic ℚ x ∧ Irrational x

/-- The strong normality conjecture: every irrational algebraic real is absolutely normal. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 41]
theorem irrational_algebraic_absolutely_normal :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ x : ℝ, IsIrrationalAlgebraic x → IsAbsolutelyNormal x := by
  sorry

/-- The weaker normality conjecture: every irrational algebraic real is normal in at least one
integer base `b ≥ 2`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11 12 41]
theorem irrational_algebraic_normal_in_some_base :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ x : ℝ, IsIrrationalAlgebraic x → ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ IsNormalInBase b x := by
  sorry

/-- Absolute normality implies normality in at least one base. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem normal_in_some_base_of_absolutely_normal {x : ℝ} (hx : IsAbsolutelyNormal x) :
    ∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ IsNormalInBase b x :=
  ⟨2, le_rfl, hx 2 le_rfl⟩

end AlgebraicNormality

findings.description: The conclusion at line 52 uses `NormalNumber.IsNormalInBase b x`, but that imported predicate (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/NormalNumber.lean:63–69) checks only single-digit frequencies: every d < b has limiting frequency 1/b. This is simple normality, not normality in base b. Thus the variant asks whether every irrational algebraic real is simply normal in some base, omitting the conditions on longer digit strings. Unlike the absolute-normality theorem, the existential base quantifier does not supply the missing conditions in all positive powers of that base. As a check on the predicate, Lean proves `IsNormalInBase 2 (1/3)` but not normality in base 2: its binary expansion is 0.010101…, so the block 00 never occurs.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number, distinguishes simple normality from normality: normality requires every n-digit string to have density b^(−n). Its Properties section states that base-b normality is equivalent to simple normality in base b^k for every positive k. Bailey–Crandall [BC01], §1 and Definition 2.1, likewise formulate algebraic absolute normality using normality for every finite digit string; read in the author-hosted manuscript at https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: With the current imported definition, replace the conclusion by `∃ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 0 < k → IsNormalInBase (b ^ k) x`. Preferably rename the existing shared predicate to `IsSimplyNormalInBase` and define genuine `IsNormalInBase` using this all-positive-powers condition, or directly using frequencies of every finite digit block.

reformulations.difference: The imported `IsAbsolutelyNormal x` requires simple normality in every integer base ≥ 2, whereas the source defines absolute normality using full normality in every such base.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These are equivalent, as Wikipedia explicitly states. For any b ≥ 2 and k > 0, b^k ≥ 2, so simple normality in every base gives simple normality in every positive power of b, which characterizes full base-b normality. Conversely, full normality implies simple normality by taking strings of length one. In scratch.lean, `absolute_iff_all_power_normality` proves the equivalence using the source's positive-powers characterization, and `strong_question_equiv` lifts it to the entire question for an arbitrary Prop-valued answer.

reformulations.difference: The written conclusion asks for simple normality in some base rather than full normality, but the absolute-normality hypothesis makes the two conclusions equivalent.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under `hx : IsAbsolutelyNormal x`, choose b = 2. For every k > 0, applying hx at base 2^k gives the positive-powers characterization of full normality in base 2. Conversely, full normality in any chosen base yields simple normality there by taking k = 1. The equivalence of these existential conclusions under hx is proved as `api_conclusion_equiv` in scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normal_number — definitions, algebraic-normality conjecture and status, equivalent characterizations, and notes.

Bailey, D. H., and Crandall, R. E., On the Random Character of Fundamental Constant Expansions [BC01], author manuscript dated 3 October 2000, §§1–2 and §7: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/baicran.pdf
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. `IsIrrationalAlgebraic` and both answer slots have the intended domains and scope. Tests cover excluded bases 0 and 1, the harmless n = 0 frequency value, terminating and negative expansions, integer-shift invariance, and nonvacuity via ±√2. The rational 1/3 example demonstrates the predicate distinction; it is not a counterexample satisfying the irrational-algebraic hypothesis. scratch.lean, digits.lean, and boundaries.lean compile successfully in /workspace/review/; the equivalence and predicate-separation proofs have no sorry dependencies. The cited Project Euclid page returned an interruption page, so BC01 was read through the author's PDF. The current Wikipedia source still records algebraic normality as open.

not_demonstrated.reason: No trivial proof or disproof of the quantified algebraic statement was established. The rational witness 1/3 distinguishes simple normality from normality, but it does not satisfy the irrationality hypothesis. Verifying that the imported predicate accepts it requires auxiliary digit-period and limiting-frequency proofs; the existing scratch proof exceeds the requested handful of lines, and finite digit computations alone would not suffice.

submission.summary: No trivial-proof file was created. The reported definition mismatch remains supported by the longer scratch proof, but no demonstration meeting this step’s brevity requirements was found.
submission.gave_up_reason: The defect weakens a noncomputable limiting-frequency assertion without making the algebraic conjecture trivially true or false. The available concrete definition counterexample requires a longer proof than this optional step permits.

submission.summary: The chosen base must now satisfy the imported digit-frequency predicate in every positive power, expressing full normality rather than simple normality. Updated the theorem's docstring to explain this characterization; other declarations and shared definitions are unchanged. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `sorry` warnings.
